caption:
Why do dark patches keep coming back even when I wear sunscreen?
One reason: SPF measures ultraviolet light, and some skin also darkens with visible light.

SPF is a burn test - mostly UVB. PA ratings and "broad spectrum" cover UVA. Neither tests the visible light you see by. For fair skin that gap matters little. For skin that tans easily, it can matter a lot.

In a lab study of 20 volunteers with skin types IV to VI, visible light produced pigmentation that was darker and lasted longer than pigment from long-wave UVA. The same light produced no pigmentation in fair skin (type II).

A small randomised trial then compared two SPF 50 sunscreens in 68 people with melasma over 8 weeks. One was tinted with iron oxide, which absorbs visible light; the other was not. The tinted group showed a 28% greater improvement in skin-colour readings. Everyone was also using the same prescription lightening cream, so this is sunscreen on top of treatment, not sunscreen alone - and on other measures the difference was smaller (15% and 4%).

So the practical version: if you tan easily and have patches that return, check whether your sunscreen is tinted. The tint is not only cosmetic. It is the part that deals with visible light. It adds to SPF and PA; it does not replace them. And patches that are spreading deserve a proper look rather than a new bottle.

Mahmoud BH et al. J Invest Dermatol 2010. doi:10.1038/jid.2010.95
Castanedo-Cazares JP et al. Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed 2014. doi:10.1111/phpp.12086

General education only.

first_comment: Most people check the SPF number and never look at whether the formula is tinted. Did you know the tint had a job?

Slide 2 of 6: UVB, UVA and visible light. Sunscreen labels are tested for the first two only.
Slide 3 of 6: 28% greater improvement in skin colour with an iron-oxide tinted SPF 50 in melasma.
Slide 4 of 6: Look for a tint, keep the SPF and PA numbers, and use enough sunscreen.
Slide 5 of 6: Visible light matters most for skin that tans easily, melasma and brown marks.
Slide 6 of 6: Protect from the light you can see - check for a tint, keep SPF and PA.
